objects.original: f, its minimizer z, x0, regularized f_delta, its minimizer, solver and complexity function phi.
objects.reconstructed: f, z, x0, delta, W, one constructed w and every approximate point x.
objects.evidence: W is exactly the regularized objective after renaming f_delta; z and w have separate global-minimizer roles. The declaration introduces neither an algorithm nor phi. Those absent objects belong to the explicitly unbound oracle-cost-class obligation.

domains.original: Unconstrained Euclidean space; real objective and parameters.
domains.reconstructed: An arbitrary proper normed additive commutative group; real objective and positive R, epsilon.
domains.evidence: Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces satisfy the Lean domain assumptions. A proper normed group need not be a real vector space, so this is a strict domain generalization, not literal source equality. The selected proof uses only compact balls, a continuous norm, and ordered real arithmetic; it never needs convex combinations or a gradient.

quantifiers.original: A class-uniform solver reduction, with comparisons for the chosen f and minimizers.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every continuous f and supplied global minimizer z, center and admissible R, epsilon, there exists one w; for every x its W-gap condition implies its f-gap bound.
quantifiers.evidence: The reconstruction accurately preserves the declaration: w is outside the all-x quantifier and is the minimizer in that same implication. No solver is existentially constructed and no uniform oracle query bound is proved. The local all-x implication validly supplies the accuracy component independently of how a solver chooses x.

assumptions.original: Convex beta-smooth Euclidean f; attained minimum and initial radius certificate; solver hypothesis.
assumptions.reconstructed: Continuous f, ProperSpace E, supplied IsMinOn f univ z, R>0, epsilon>0, and norm(z-x0)<=R.
assumptions.evidence: Source smoothness implies continuity and Euclidean closed balls are compact. Thus the explicit analytic assumptions impose no additional condition on the intended Euclidean instances. Convexity, smoothness constants and a solver are unnecessary for this comparison component. Positive R makes division genuine; R=0 is outside this declaration and can be handled separately by the already optimal center. This is an explicit boundary, not a source correction.

conclusion.original: Algorithmic reduction; its proof includes radius and epsilon-accuracy comparisons.
conclusion.reconstructed: Existence of a global W-minimizer, sharp radius comparison, and uniform half-error transfer.
conclusion.evidence: The three supported obligations are exactly regularized-minimum, radius-comparison and accuracy-transfer. The local construction is stronger than merely assuming that w exists. It does not establish strong convexity, smoothness, an implementable first-order algorithm, or the advertised class-uniform complexity. Accordingly this is accepted as a proof component, never as all of Lemma 4.2.

scopes.original: Section 4.1 uses successful optimization in a first-order oracle model.
scopes.reconstructed: IsMinOn over Set.univ and real-valued objective inequalities; no operational oracle semantics.
scopes.evidence: Both minimizers are global, not local or constrained. The compact-ball step is only a proof device; the following outside-ball comparison upgrades it to a global minimum. The authored lesson and module explicitly exclude curvature and oracle costs, matching the binding scope. The minimum is not supplied as an algorithm output.

constant_dependencies.original: delta=epsilon/R^2, two epsilon/2 terms, radius R; beta and phi in the remaining reduction.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same delta and half-error factors, norm(w-x0)<=norm(z-x0)<=R, no beta or phi.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The transfer constant is exactly one: the regularization penalty at z is at most epsilon/2 and the approximate W-gap is at most epsilon/2. No dimension or compactness constant enters. The declaration applies for all positive epsilon, since the condition epsilon<=beta R^2 is needed only by the remaining condition-number comparison.

review_evidence: Independent review of the anti-anchored packet and primary source https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S4.SS1, including the Section 4.1 opening definition and Lemma 4.2 statement/proof. I read neither the old registry nor previous review verdicts. The blind reconstruction matches the supplied elaborated Lean statement. I inspected the entire module text and authored lesson in this packet. Its compact-ball existence proof is valid: choose a minimizer on the closed ball containing z; outside the ball, global minimality of z and the radial penalty give W(z)<=W(x), so the chosen point minimizes globally. Comparing its value with W(z) and using f(z)<=f(w) cancels the positive coefficient to give the sharp norm inequality. Nonnegative penalty and the radius certificate then yield the advertised all-x implication. No hidden differentiability, convexity, uniqueness, or oracle hypothesis is used. The candidate publication statement is a faithful contextual paraphrase, while its binding and lesson expressly claim only three components. Its two remaining obligations are correctly uncovered. Acceptance is for that component publication; the verdict is lean-weakened-conclusion relative to the entire pinned source statement, not full-source equivalence. No source repair is necessary. Compiler success was supplied in the packet and was not independently rerun by this source-review role.
